title: Launch Conductor: capacity signal framework and contingency lanes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we scale coordinated launches across runtime/console/api, teams face ambiguous capacity boundaries and manual coordination overhead. This ticket defines a machine-readable 'capacity signal' and a set of contingency lanes that the release conductor uses to accept, delay, or reroute launch traffic.

Scope: design the capacity signal spec (3-state + quantitative bands), wire a proof-of-concept propagation path from capacity forecasting -> calendar -> conductor, and build a minimal UI in Console to surface signals and suggested mitigation actions. Integrations: Dedicated autoscaler, routing policies in the router, and the launch calendar service (calendar-as-code). Not in scope: full autoscaler rewrite or new billing model changes.

Goal: reduce manual cross-team coordination time during cutover by 60% and decrease launch-related rollback incidents by 40% in the first two quarters after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity signal spec published in Confluence and approved by infra/eng/product
Conductor reads signal and enforces one of three actions (Proceed/Throttle/Hold) in canary windows
Console UI surfaces the current signal and recommended mitigations with a one-click 'apply mitigation' for SREs
End-to-end demo: a staged runtime change triggers amber signal, conductor throttles canary traffic, and rollback aborts automated promotion
Metrics: playbook runbook tests show >=60% reduction in manual coordination steps vs baseline
